column2: High Broker Partition Count - Leading unresponsive cluster, causing connection latency
column3:
Cluster will be overloaded due to which cluster can go unresponsive and cause application downtime. Prevents operations like: Update the cluster configuration,
 Update the Apache Kafka version for the cluster,
 Update the cluster to a smaller broker type,
 Associate an AWS Secrets Manager secret with a cluster that has SASL/SCRAM authentication, Missing Kafka metrics on CloudWatch and on Prometheus scraping
column5:
Creating topics without proper planning as per best practices
 Setting unnecessarily high replication factors.
 Maintaining unused topics that consume resources.
Uneven/skewed partition distribution strategies. Lack of regular monitoring and rebalancing. Over-partitioning without considering actual throughput needs. Underestimating resource requirements during cluster planning.
column7:
CloudWatch Metrics: 
1. PartitionCount: Primary metric for tracking partition numbers, create alerts when this metric approaches or exceeds recommended limits 
2. LeaderCount: Useful for identifying imbalances in partition distribution, create alerts for unexpected spikes or disproportionate leader counts. 
3. UnderMinIsrPartitionCount: High values for this metric can be related to excessive partitioning and underreplicated partitions, create alerts for non-zero values or increasing trends.
4. UnderReplicatedPartitions: Can be symptomatic of overloaded brokers due to high partition counts, create alerts for non-zero values or sudden increases. 
5. ProduceTotalTimeMsMean: Increasing values of this metric may indicate strain from high partition counts, create alerts for significant increases above baseline. 
6. NetworkRxPackets/NetworkRxErrors: High partition counts can lead to increased network traffic, create lerts for unusual spikes in either metric. 
7. TrustedAdvisor: Check TA regulalry. MSK Monitoring guide
column10:
Carefully plan the number of brokers based on MSK best practices. Consider upgrading to larger broker types if needed.
Keep partition numbers proportional to actual workload requirements. Aim for an even distribution of partitions across brokers.
Use CloudWatch metrics to track partition counts. Set up alerts for approaching partition limits. Periodically reassess and rebalance partition distribution.
Use kafka-reassign-partitions.sh for manual rebalancing. Limit reassignments to 10-20 partitions per operation for safety.
Remove unused topics to free up resources. Consolidate topics with low throughput. Consider using compacted topics where appropriate.
Explore MSK Serverless for automatic partition management. Use MSK tiered storage to offload older data.
Add more brokers to spread partition load. 
Expand cluster size in a balanced manner across Availability Zones.
Set appropriate retention periods for topics. Use log compaction where applicable to manage data growth.
Design consumer groups efficiently to avoid unnecessary partitions. Balance consumer group counts with partition counts.

column2: High Offline Partition Count - Leads to disruption in streaming operations.
column3: Inability to read/write affected partitions. Potential data access failures. Increased latency in message processing. Resource contention on remaining active partitions. Potential application timeouts. Reduced overall cluster throughput. Risk of complete service outages.
column5: Insufficient disk space for partition data. EBS volume performance issues. DNS resolution failures. Improper replication factor settings. Incorrect min.insync.replicas configuration. Excessive partition counts overwhelming brokers. Underlying EC2 instance performance(CPU, Memory, I/O). Network disruptions in VPC or cross-AZ. Replica lag leading to out-of-sync partitions.
column7:
CloudWatch Metrics: 
1. OfflinePartitionsCount: Tracks total number of offline partitions cluster-wide, critical metric requiring immediate attention if >0. Set Warning alarm when first offline partition detected. Set Critical alarm when count exceeds >1. Set Emergency alarm for sustained offline partition states. 
2. GlobalTopicCount/GlobalPartitionCount: These metrics represents total topic and partition counts cluster wide, steady increase or spike in these metrics needs attention.
3. KafkaDataLogsDiskUsed: These metrics represents storage usage by Kafka brokers, low free space blocks partition growth.
4. NetworkTxPackets/NetworkRxPackets: Indicates Network transmission health and connectivity issues which can lead to offline partition.
5. CpuIoWait/CpuSystem/CpuUser/MemoryFree: CPU/Memory usage metrics, indicates resource preassure which can lead to offline partition. 
6. VolumeQueueLength: EBS volume queue depth which can cause I/O latency and I/O preassure leading to offline parition.
7. UnderReplicatedPartitions: Indicates number of under replicated paritions in a broker, configure alarm if the value is > 0 continuesly or there is sustained spike in this metric.
column10:
Keep partitions within recommended limits per broker and plan partition counts before topic creation. 
Maintain even partition distribution across brokers.
Implement Cruise Control for automated balancing.
Use kafka-reassign-partitions.sh carefully (max 10 at once).
Remove unused topics regularly and set alarms for Storage, CPU, Memory and Network metrics in MSK.
Maintain balanced broker distribution across AZs.
Use automatic stotrage scaling for standard broker clusters.
Explore MSK Serverless for automatic partition management. Use MSK tiered storage to offload older data or use Express brokers for automatic storage management. 
Scale MSK cluster/or storage to add more resources to accomodate offline paritions.

Memory pressure in controller nodes leading to frequent GC pauses.
Improper ZooKeeper session timeout settings and misconfigured broker settings.

column7:
CloudWatch Metrics: 
1. ActiveControllerCount: Indicates number of brokers currently acting as the cluster controller, a value other than 1, either 0 or greater than 1, signifies a problem.
2. OfflinePartitionsCount: Tracks total number of offline partitions cluster-wide, critical metric requiring immediate attention if >0, high OfflinePartitionsCount can be a symptom of an issue leading to frequent active controller fluctuations.
3. ZooKeeperSessionState: Indicates broker's ZooKeeper connection status, set alarm if there is frequent spike in this metric. 
4. ZooKeeperRequestLatencyMsMean: Indicates mean latency in milliseconds for Apache ZooKeeper requests from broker, high latency can lead to conrtoller instability. 
5. KafkaDataLogsDiskUsed: indicates percentage of disk space used for data logs, high storage usage leads to low free storage and broker instability.
column10:
Set alarm for ActiveControllerCount and related metrics like OfflinePartitionsCount, ZooKeeperSessionState, KafkaDataLogsDiskUsed, NetworkRxPackets and NetworkRxErrors.
Tune ZooKeeper session timeout settings and monitor network throughout metrics for high usage.
Scale MSK cluster/or storage to add more resources, use automatic stotrage scaling for standard broker clusters.
Consider MSK Serverless for automatic management of controller elections and cluster scaling.
Consider cross-region replication for critical workloads to address multiple active controller failures.

column7:
CloudWatch Metrics:
1. CpuSystem/CpuUser: Indicates percentage of CPU in kernel space and user space, combined usage of these metrics above 60% is a concern. 
2. CpuIoWait: Indicates percentage of CPU idle time during a pending disk operation, a sustained high value indicates I/O bottleneck.
3. MemoryFree: Indicates size in bytes of memory that is free and available for the broker, low memory memory can lead to increased CPU load due to swapping.
4. HeapMemoryAfterGC: Indicates percentage of total heap memory in use after garbage collection, high value of this metric can indirectly cause high CPU usage, set alarm if the value crosses 60%.
5. ActiveControllerCount: Indicates number of brokers currently acting as the cluster controller, spikes may correlate with CPU spikes.

Happens when request rates are too high for a bucket. 
Typically occurs when exceeding service limits (3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE or 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned prefix).

CloudWatch Metrics:
1. 5xxErrors: Tracks overall server-side error responses. Monitors frequency of internal server errors. Can be used to calculate error rates.
2. TotalRequestLatency: Indicates elapsed per-request time from the first byte received to the last byte sent to an Object Lambda Access Point. This metric includes the time taken to receive the request body and send the response body, which is not included in FirstByteLatency.
3. FirstByteLatency: Indicates the per-request time from the complete request being received by an Amazon S3 bucket to when the response starts to be returned.
